summary: Fictional example: every post, author, id and URL in this corpus is invented, and any resemblance to real people, posts or companies is coincidental. First-time founders in this window talk about getting a meeting more than about any other part of the raise. Warm introductions work as the gate: practitioners tell founders to skip cold email, and founders without a network say they cannot get meetings even with paying customers. The second escalated pain is the proof bar, where practitioners contradict each other on how much traction a pre-seed round needs. Accelerators appear both as a way in front of investors and as programmes founders doubt.

personas.name: First-time founder raising a first round without investor connections
personas.context: Pre-seed, first company, posting in r/startups and r/venturecapital, often with early revenue or letters of intent

anti_personas.segment: Founders with strong traction who reach funds directly
anti_personas.reason: They get meetings without introductions; the access pain is not theirs.

recommendations.text: Test founder-facing copy that leads with getting the first investor meeting, in the founders' words, against copy that leads with the programme content.
recommendations.falsified_if: The access-led variant converts no better on the same traffic, or the next watch run shows the access pain falling.

recommendations.text: Publish a sourced piece on what proof pre-seed investors ask for, since practitioners in the corpus contradict each other on the bar.
recommendations.falsified_if: Readers' replies say the bar was already clear to them, or the piece draws less engagement than the account's usual posts.

recommendations.text: Answer the programme doubts on the application page with what the programme can show, before using introductions as a selling point.
recommendations.falsified_if: Applicants never raise programme quality or introductions in their questions.

limitations: Fictional example: the corpus, the recorded API answers, the authors, ids and URLs were written to show the agent's output and describe no real post, person or company.
English sources only; no French community was collected in this run.
Reddit comes from the Arctic Shift archive: deleted comments are absent and the most recent days may be missing.
The App Store feed returned no review for Tablesplit in this run, so there is no review mining.
Hacker News search for the exact phrase pre-seed returns mostly hiring threads; Stack Exchange has no active startup site.
